concerns.text: Task T023 restricts centrality calculation to 'FIXED regions (AAL indices 1-10)' and explicitly forbids calculating metrics for 'all regions'. This violates spec FR-002 which mandates computing metrics for 'each subject's functional connectivity matrix derived from a standard atlas' (implying the full ~90 regions) and plan.md Task 1.3 which requires calculating metrics for the full matrix before aggregation. The task silently weakens the requirement to compute full-matrix centrality.

Task T024 aggregates a 'global centrality' score from the 'fixed subset' (10 regions) defined in T023. Spec FR-002.1 requires aggregating 'regional centrality metrics' (plural, implying the full set) into a global score. By restricting the input to only 10 regions, the task fails to satisfy the requirement to aggregate the full set of regional metrics, effectively weakening the aggregation scope.

Task T026 calculates VIF for 'degree, betweenness, eigenvector' metrics derived from T023 (10 regions). Spec Edge Cases and plan Task 1.6 require detecting collinearity for the predictors used in the global model. If the global model is intended to represent the full network (as per FR-002), calculating VIF on a 10-region subset does not validate the collinearity of the full network metrics, creating a semantic gap in the validation logic.

Task T032 implements 'Conditional Regional Analysis' that triggers only if 'global_model_p_value > 0.05'. Spec FR-004.1 states 'If regional-level analysis is performed, System MUST apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction'. The task logic creates a conditional trigger that might prevent the analysis (and thus the required FDR correction) from ever running if the global model is significant, potentially violating the requirement to correct *if* the analysis is performed, as the analysis itself is now gated by a result that might not exist.

Task T037 describes 'Cross-Validation' but the description focuses on comparing against a baseline R². Spec FR-005 and US-3 Acceptance Scenario 2 explicitly require 'k-fold cross-validation' to 'report out-of-sample prediction accuracy (R² and RMSE) and standard deviation'. The task description lacks explicit mention of the k-fold mechanism, out-of-sample calculation, and standard deviation reporting, risking a silent omission of these acceptance criteria.
